questions.title: Checking if it’s your ball
questions.question: When can you pick up your ball to see if it’s really yours?

choices.text: Only if your ball is on the green
If you mark where it is first and you need to check
Never, you always have to hit it where it sits
Only if the other player says you can

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your ball is yours, you must put a marker down to show where it is, then you can pick it up and look. You can do this anywhere on the course, not just on the green.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A small object (like a coin) you put down to remember where your ball was.
The smooth, short grass area around the hole.
The whole area where you play golf.

questions.teachingTip: Show how to mark a ball with a coin before lifting it, and remind children that they must always put the ball back in the same spot.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can only check their ball on the green.
Some may believe they never need to mark the spot before picking up their ball.
Some might think they always need an opponent’s permission.

questions.title: Identifying your ball
questions.question: When are you allowed to lift your golf ball to check if it is yours?

choices.text: Only if it is on the putting green
If you first mark its position and need to identify it
Never; you must always play it as it lies

questions.explanation: If you cannot identify your ball, you may mark its position and lift it anywhere on the course to check – not just on the putting green.
